Tracking down the Table Mountain Killer

By: Annalise Lubbe | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In 2017 and 2018, a spate of muggings, stabbings and murders occurred in the Table Mountain Reserve. We find out how ‘eyes and ears on the ground’ helped to identify the suspected killer.

Unique Selling Point:
Table Mountain Reserve has always been a place of beauty and tranquility for hikers and cyclists. But all this changed in 2017 and 2018 when a man by the name of Blessing Bveni used the park as his hotspot to ambush and kill unsuspected hikers and cyclists. His appearance was misleading as he was dressed as someone who is going for a stroll in the reserve and with a kind smile. This would all change when he would suddenly take out his knife or screwdriver and lunge towards the person slashing and stabbing in a bout of anger that has turned him into a monster. It took two years to gather enough evidence and put him behind bars. He is currently awaiting trial.

Summary:
Zimbabwean national Blessing Bveni is linked to the series of muggings and stabbings in the Silvermine Nature reserve above Kalk Bay and St James before he was arrested for the murders of pilot Doug Notten on January 28, 2018 and pensioner Ian McPherson, stabbed to death for his bicycle on March 13, 2018.

In an ongoing trial in the Western Cape High Court the State alleges Bveni was involved in a number of attacks on cyclists and hikers before he killed Notten, 57, who was hiking with his wife, Julia in Silvermine above their St James home and McPerson who was cycling on the Fish Hoek side of Silvermine. Bveni is also accused of repeatedly stabbing and robbing neighbourhood watch member Malcolm Esterhuizen on February 7, 1918 at the exact spot where McPerson was killed.


Further information:
It was round about nine in the morning when neighbourhood watch member Esterhuizen did his patrol on the outskirts of the Fish Hoek residential area. With him was his faithful dog and his radio control. He took a phone call from a friend of his - not the usual thing he would do whilst on patrol - when a man approached him from the opposite side of the footpath. Being a narrow path, he stepped out of the way for him to pass. The man was dressed neatly and had a kind smile. The next moment he felt a firm hand on him and was thrown to the ground. In a flash he saw a screwdriver in the hand of the attacker and he knew this was trouble. In the seventies Esterhuizen did a bit of karate and knew how to do basic movements to defend himself but this man had an anger in him that was uncontrollable. His lung was punctured and he was stabbed multiple times in the front and back. Eventually the attacker grabbed the cellphone and the radio and ran off with the stolen goods. Fortunately for Esterhuizen his cellphone remained switched on during the attack which alerted his friend of the emergency to send the police and medical assistance. Esterhuizen was treated for multiple stab wounds but recovered and was able to give a clear description of his attacker. He has since been back on patrol and has testified in court as a witness who could clearly identify Bvendi as the attacker.

In a Carte Blanche story of February 2018 we interviewed Julia Notten after her husband Doug was killed on a morning hike in the reserve. She escaped and ran for help but by the time the paramedics were back with Doug he passed away. She too was able to identify Bveni in court as the man who murdered her husband.

In another incident, Stephen Howells, a baker from Fish Hoek was jogging his regular route on the outskirts of Fish Hoek in the same area where Esterhuizen was stabbed. A man on a bicycle was cycling towards him coming from the opposite direction. Howells took a good look at him and saw that he was in a great hurry to pass. He jumped out of the way but in the process the man bumped into him and then rushed past. Howell continued jogging and about 50 meters further he heard a calling for help. An elderly man, later identified as Ian McPerson, was lying in the grass with several stab wounds on his body and was gasping for air. He came closer and saw the gushes of the stabwounds - his intestines were bulging out. He tried to make him comfortable and ran for help. Back in the street he managed to stop an oncoming car and asked the driver to call emergency services to help the dying man. But it was too late, McPerson died within minutes after the paramedics arrived. The attacker stole McPerson’s bicycle, his phone and a watch.

Our story:
We will recap on the story we covered in 2018 when Doug Notten was murdered and his wife Julia spoke about the senseless killing. The story will then pick up with the added death of Ian McPerson and the identification of Bveni with the help of Stephen Howells and Malcolm Esterhuizen who gave a positive identification of Bveni. We will also interview Pete McPherson and his sisters who will give us a sense of who Ian was and the legacy he left behind as a man who never wanted to be a victim but rather unite people when a tragic event like this occurs. In addition some footage of the court case will be included.

We have requested an interview with SANParks to speak to a Sergeant Minye who helped to identify the route the offender took after he stole the bicycle but was declined due to the trial still ongoing and fearing for his safety.
We have also requested an interview with SAPS who have declined for the same reason - the trial is still ongoing.

Script:


FINAL Script: Tracking down the Table Mountain killer
Duration: 6 minutes
Date: 15 October 2020


V/O It was about 9 am on the 7th of February in 2018 when Malcolm Esterhuizen went on his usual patrol in the neighbourhood of Fish Hoek.

Up sound: ON WALKIE TALKIE.“Justin come in …”

V/O Esterhuizen was talking to a friend on his cellphone when a man approached from the opposite direction.

Malcolm Esterhuizen - Victim: When he drew level with me he barged me off my feet and when I was flat on my back... he launched an attack on me with a screwdriver. He lunged at me, I don’t know, 15, 20 times. The last two was pretty serious.

V/O The attacker fled with Esterhuizen’s phone, the radio and his watch. Esterhuizen was rushed to False bay hospital and later gave police his attacker’s description.

Up sound old programme

V/O In February 2018 Carte Blanche reported on several incidents of stabbings and muggings on hikers in the Table Mountain National Park in Silvermine area.

Up sound: ….what is your emergency?

V/O On 28 January 2018, 57-Year old Douglas Notten and his wife Julia went for their usual hike above Kalk Bay.

Julia Notten - Victim’s wife: I saw all of a sudden that man behind him….and then he pulled out a very very big knife and hammered it into his shoulders and neck and that is when I just turned around and ran away.

V/O Notten died from multiple stab wounds. Julia was able to sketch the attacker for the police.

V/O On 13 March 2018 Stephen Howells - a resident from Glencairn – was running through the same stretch of veld where Esterhuizen’s attack occurred a month earlier.

Stephen Howells - Witness: I saw this man coming towards me and I saw he was riding a really expensive mountain bike.

V/O He passed the man, and only meters later discovered a grizzly sight.

Stephen Howells: He was on his side, I knelt down to him, grabbed his arms, he was trying to communicate with me. He had a stab wound on the front of his chest and above his heart..

V/O Howells ran for help, returning within minutes.

Stephen Howells: I was holding his hand. He was trying to hang on. I was just trying to reassure him “you are going to be ok, you would be ok.”

V/O Howells could hear ambulance sirens responding.

Stephen Howells: Eventually he just passed away and his grip just went.

V/O Ian McPherson (pronounced Mac-fur-sin), a local from Fish Hoek was one of five siblings, says his brother Peter.

Peter McPherson - Victim’s brother: He was not only my brother but my best friend and I miss him so much. My sisters have been very strong and the community of Fish Hoek had been great.

V/O A memorial bicycle was erected in honour of McPherson on Fish Hoek beach by the cycling fraternity including Renford Brand.

Renford Brand - Victim’s friend: He actually saved my life. When I lost my leg one morning going Ou Kaapse Weg. I had a very nasty accident. He applied first aid immediately.

V/O Police recovered McPherson’s bicycle in a nearby township known as Masiphumelele leading them to a suspect known as Blessing Bveni who also had several other items of the victims. Esterhuizen, Howell and Notten positively identified Bveni, and a shirt collected from his house matched McPherson’s DNA, leading to Bveni’s arrest on March 3rd 2018. He was charged with robbery, attempted murder and murder amongst others.

V/O The trial began in February this year. While it is ongoing SANParks and the police have declined to comment. At the Western Cape High Court, presided over by Honourable Judge Judie Cloete, Bveni’s Attorney Henk Carstens, cross-examined police officers and attempted to poke holes in the state’s case, because the collection of the shirt linking Bveni to McPherson’s attack, had taken police several days to enter into evidence.

Defence Attorney: The description of the item brought in was a blue coloured shirt? On what date did you book it in?
Witness’ response: 5 days later.

V/O Bveni testified on Wednesday, maintaining his innocence on all charges, including Notton’s murder.

Defense Attorney: Count 6 relates to the murder - it happens in Silvermine Nature Reserve of Mr. Notten. It is alleged that you stabbed and killed him.

Blessing Bveni: Accused “It is not true I did not murder him.”

V/O State Advocate Christopher Burke cross-examined Bveni - pressing him about the attack on Esterhuizen.

State Prosecutor: He said you, Mr Bveni attacked him in Brigantine road with a screwdriver with a black and yellow handle on.

Blessing Bveni: “It’’s not true, I’ve never been close to that area.”

State Prosecutor: He says you tried to stab him about 12 times.

Blessing Bveni: “It wasn’t me…”

Malcolm Esterhuizen: I am certain he will be convicted on the strength of what he did to Ian McPherson and to Doug Notten and to myself. It is just sad that they can't be here to tell you about their attacks as well and somebody should talk for them.

V/O The defense may still call other witnesses to give further evidence in support of Bveni's case. Arguments have been set down for October 26th. Only then will the judge decide whether he is guilty or not.

V/O Julia Notten declined an interview - but these were her words afer her husband’s murder.

Julia Notten: He was peaceful. He had a bunch of flowers in his hands.

V/O: McPherson's wife Allyn (wants to be referred to as "Ayleen" and not Allyn) and son Rob have since left the country.

Allyn McPerson: Victim’s wife - I have got to say this. I have learnt not to focus on the past of what I have lost. I try and focus on what I had and what I still have.

Rob McPherson: Victim’s son - A son could not have asked for a better father. He was the backbone of the family, backbone of the community.

V/o The senseless nature of the attacks left the surrounding community residents fearful to hike. But Brand still cycles in memory of his friend, McPherson.

Renford Brand: Every time I get on my bike, every time and ride I think of him.

Promos:
● In 2018 Table Mountain Reserve became a horror scene when a man went on a rampage stabbing and mugging people. A suspect is now on trial for double murder.

● In 2018 Table Mountain Reserve became a place of terror when a slew of knife attacks occurred. A suspect has now been charged and could face life behind bars if found guilty.

● Two years ago an attacker went on a rampage stabbing hikers and cyclists in the Table Mountain Reserve. The suspect is now on trial on a double murder.

This would all change when he would suddenly take out his knife or screwdriver and lunge towards the person slashing and stabbing in a bout of anger that has turned him into a monster. It took two years to gather enough evidence and put him behind bars. He is currently awaiting trial.
metadata.Summary: Zimbabwean national Blessing Bveni is linked to the series of muggings and stabbings in the Silvermine Nature reserve above Kalk Bay and St James before he was arrested for the murders of pilot Doug Notten on January 28, 2018 and pensioner Ian McPherson, stabbed to death for his bicycle on March 13, 2018. In an ongoing trial in the Western Cape High Court the State alleges Bveni was involved in a number of attacks on cyclists and hikers before he killed Notten, 57, who was hiking with his wife, Julia in Silvermine above their St James home and McPerson who was cycling on the Fish Hoek side of Silvermine. Bveni is also accused of repeatedly stabbing and robbing neighbourhood watch member Malcolm Esterhuizen on February 7, 1918 at the exact spot where McPerson was killed.
metadata.Further information: It was round about nine in the morning when neighbourhood watch member Esterhuizen did his patrol on the outskirts of the Fish Hoek residential area. With him was his faithful dog and his radio control. He took a phone call from a friend of his - not the usual thing he would do whilst on patrol - when a man approached him from the opposite side of the footpath. Being a narrow path, he stepped out of the way for him to pass. The man was dressed neatly and had a kind smile. The next moment he felt a firm hand on him and was thrown to the ground. In a flash he saw a screwdriver in the hand of the attacker and he knew this was trouble. In the seventies Esterhuizen did a bit of karate and knew how to do basic movements to defend himself but this man had an anger in him that was uncontrollable. His lung was punctured and he was stabbed multiple times in the front and back. Eventually the attacker grabbed the cellphone and the radio and ran off with the stolen goods. Fortunately for Esterhuizen his cellphone remained switched on during the attack which alerted his friend of the emergency to send the police and medical assistance. Esterhuizen was treated for multiple stab wounds but recovered and was able to give a clear description of his attacker. He has since been back on patrol and has testified in court as a witness who could clearly identify Bvendi as the attacker. In a Carte Blanche story of February 2018 we interviewed Julia Notten after her husband Doug was killed on a morning hike in the reserve. She escaped and ran for help but by the time the paramedics were back with Doug he passed away. She too was able to identify Bveni in court as the man who murdered her husband. In another incident, Stephen Howells, a baker from Fish Hoek was jogging his regular route on the outskirts of Fish Hoek in the same area where Esterhuizen was stabbed. A man on a bicycle was cycling towards him coming from the opposite direction. Howells took a good look at him and saw that he was in a great hurry to pass. He jumped out of the way but in the process the man bumped into him and then rushed past. Howell continued jogging and about 50 meters further he heard a calling for help. An elderly man, later identified as Ian McPerson, was lying in the grass with several stab wounds on his body and was gasping for air. He came closer and saw the gushes of the stabwounds - his intestines were bulging out. He tried to make him comfortable and ran for help. Back in the street he managed to stop an oncoming car and asked the driver to call emergency services to help the dying man. But it was too late, McPerson died within minutes after the paramedics arrived. The attacker stole McPerson’s bicycle, his phone and a watch. Our story: We will recap on the story we covered in 2018 when Doug Notten was murdered and his wife Julia spoke about the senseless killing. The story will then pick up with the added death of Ian McPerson and the identification of Bveni with the help of Stephen Howells and Malcolm Esterhuizen who gave a positive identification of Bveni. We will also interview Pete McPherson and his sisters who will give us a sense of who Ian was and the legacy he left behind as a man who never wanted to be a victim but rather unite people when a tragic event like this occurs. In addition some footage of the court case will be included. We have requested an interview with SANParks to speak to a Sergeant Minye who helped to identify the route the offender took after he stole the bicycle but was declined due to the trial still ongoing and fearing for his safety. We have also requested an interview with SAPS who have declined for the same reason - the trial is still ongoing.
